prior_orchestrator_verdict.rationale: All three lenses ran; acceptance passes every story AC and spec item S1-S7 (all 7 delete paths confirmed to go through IndexInfo.delete()). One major patch: the JSONB contains payload that drives the whole cleanup is never exercised in any test, so an under-match (e.g. enum not serialised to its value) would silently make B a no-op. Deferred (3): no row lock between select and write (same as the skill-cleanup precedent), guard-to-update TOCTOU window, index delete and assistant update not atomic; all three are covered at runtime by option A. Dismissed (10): guard ordering (base delete commits in its own session first), Context equality/raw dicts (Context.__eq__ + PydanticListType returns models), cross-project refs (verified impossible), legacy context items dropped on write (same as any assistant save; those items are already ignored on load), broad except (mirrors the scheduler cleanup in the same method), naive datetime (matches base.py), exact-name match, old versions (out of scope, option A), missing log assertion and __future__ import (minor).

findings.title: JSONB contains payload never verified
findings.problem: Tests mock Session and only check column names in the compiled WHERE clause; the bound payload [{name, context_type}] (with a ContextType enum inside) is never asserted, and no test runs the predicate against Postgres.
findings.impact: If the payload under-matches (enum serialised as name, wrong key), the SELECT returns nothing and B silently becomes a no-op while every test stays green.
findings.recommendation: Add a unit test that compiles the statement with the postgresql dialect and asserts the bound JSON payload equals [{"name": "kb-x", "context_type": "knowledge_base"}]; confirm end-to-end in `make test-harness` before undrafting.

prior_orchestrator_verdict.rationale: CR-001 resolved: new test compiles the query for the postgresql dialect and asserts the bound JSONB payload equals [{name, context_type:"knowledge_base"}]; mutation (enum name instead of value) makes it fail. Fix-up diff (test + __future__ import) introduces no new high-risk issue, so no confirmation pass was needed.
